Per Rule 1 conservative inference, absorbed_kelvin_risk = min(6, board_kelvin_net_count) >= 2; with zero Kelvin nets in output this dispatch should have been blocked. rule_enforcement_failures must be incremented; if it reaches 3, escalate without dispatching.

New structural finding (not covered by existing rules): the directed stubs are allocated exclusively to CONTROL nets (CAN_H, I2C_SCL, I2C_SDA) that do NOT appear in failing_reasons, while the chronically failing Kelvin nets /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO received zero stub support. This allocation is inverted — the stub mechanism is providing directed routing assistance to nets that FR already routes successfully, while the nets that have failed across multiple rounds receive no stub foothold. Existing rules (1, 7, 11) prevent Kelvin stubs from being ABSORBED after they are generated, and kelvin_force_recheck ensures their coordinates are re-derived. But none of the standing rules mandate that Kelvin nets appearing in failing_reasons must be INJECTED INTO the compiler's input as mandatory stub candidates in the first place. The gap is at stub generation, not stub survival. This explains the persistent pattern: the absorber exclusion list protects stubs that were never generated.

No new scorer metric is warranted. kelvin_unrouted=1000 and gate_fail=1000 are already strong penalty signals; the issue is not incentive magnitude but stub generation priority. Adding more weight would not change the routing topology or fix the stub allocation inversion.
manager_rule: After any round where a /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO net appears in failing_reasons with the phrase 'has unconnected ratlines', the manager MUST add both /SENSEC{N}_HI and /SENSEC{N}_LO to a persistent set named 'kelvin_stub_priority' that survives across round boundaries. Before the stub compiler runs in the next round, every net in kelvin_stub_priority MUST be injected into the compiler's input as a mandatory stub candidate, with stub coordinates re-derived from the current board netlist per Rule 4. If the compiler's stub slot capacity requires dropping candidates, stubs for nets in kelvin_stub_priority take precedence over all control and signal nets (including /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA, and any net not currently in failing_reasons). After compilation, if any net in kelvin_stub_priority is absent from the final stub nets list AND absent from compile_failures, the manager MUST treat this as a compile_failure for that net by name and abort the FR dispatch per Rule 3 — this condition is distinct from the Rule 7 zero-Kelvin-in-output check and fires even when other Kelvin nets are present in the output. A net is removed from kelvin_stub_priority only after a round in which it does not appear in failing_reasons (confirmed routed). This rule operates at stub GENERATION time; it complements but does not replace the Rule 1 absorber exclusion list (which operates at stub SURVIVAL time).
